finding: Canonical inner publication is not a byte-only pg<g04 comparison. PrefixGraph must first be strictly smaller than complete G0-G4 and then pass authenticated-metadata locality; otherwise G0-G4 remains selected.
exact_current_law: If pg_bytes >= g04_bytes, PrefixGraph is rejected as complete-artifact-not-smaller.
If pg_bytes < g04_bytes, canonical admission computes PrefixGraph locality from authenticated metadata.
PrefixGraph publishes only when locality.passed is true; a smaller nonlocal PrefixGraph candidate is rejected as locality-ceiling.
All-direct PrefixGraph has no prefix dependencies and therefore has 1.0 member-read amplification, but it must still remain an explicit candidate in the proof tournament.
staged_r1_rule: Build the unchanged process-owned PrefixGraph reference and record its exact bytes/SHA/anchor plus canonical locality verdict.
Define the reference final inner winner as PrefixGraph only when pg_bytes < g04_bytes AND locality.passed; otherwise select G0-G4.
On PrefixGraph-winning controls, the proof arm must reproduce the exact reference PrefixGraph bytes/SHA/anchor; identical bytes imply identical locality.

On G0-G4-winning controls, a proof arm may only claim selection identity after accounting for both exact complete bytes and canonical locality. Do not treat a smaller but locality-red PrefixGraph reference as a product winner.

The cross-representation anchor lower-bound terminal remains sound at lower_bound >= complete_g04_bytes because such an anchor cannot satisfy the necessary strict-byte condition for publication regardless of locality.
claim_boundary: Evidence-specification correction only. No product code, threshold, locality ceiling, grammar, reader, selector or release authority changes.
